clues: This city sits in the north-west of Senegal in West Africa. It lies near the mouth of a river that shares the country's name.
Climate change is pushing sea levels up, and the rising water threatens the city centre. A study says up to 80% of the city could be at risk of flooding by 2080.
It was the capital of the French colony here from 1673 until 1902. Then that role was moved to Dakar.
From 1920 to 1957, it did a strange double job. It was the capital of the next-door colony of Mauritania too.
UNESCO named its old town a World Heritage Site in 2000. That honour helps draw the crowds who come here as tourists.
